newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Ganges water sharing treaty between India and Bangladesh goes into effect on Wednesday with the beginning of joint monitoring of the flow of the mighty international river.
Former Prime Minister and opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia said the 1996 would be marked as a year of "selling out of the country's political independence as well as territorial sovereignty".

Opposition BNP Secretary General Abdl Mannan Bhuiyan has warned the governemnt that his party would "soon build resistance instead just protesting" against the "conspiracy" to run the parliament without the main opposition.
The government has identified 108 industrial units in the public sector for privatisation. Of those, 65 units will be trasnferred by June this year.
The ceasefire in the Chittagong Hills Tracts has been extended upto March 31 this year, an official announcement said on Tuesday.
Propspect for a good Boro crop in Bangladesh has improved with increased availability of water and fertiliser, said a "Rice Situation Update" released by FAO.
Bangladesh pavilion has secured "overall best award" in the Industrial India Trade Fair' 96 which ended in Calcutta on Tuesday.
